n: Isaiah 8: God tells Isaiah to write in large, plain letters the name “Maher-shalal-hash-baz,” meaning “swift to plunder, quick to spoil” — a warning that Assyria would soon loot Syria and Israel.

f.g: Hebrew “quick to the plunder, swift to the spoil.”

n: Isaiah has two reliable witnesses confirm the writing, so when the prophecy comes true, no one can deny it was given beforehand.
Isaiah’s wife, called “the prophetess,” bears a son, and God tells them to give him this prophetic name.

f.g: Isaiah’s wife; perhaps a prophet in her own right.

n: Before the baby can say “Daddy” or “Mommy,” Assyria will plunder Damascus and Samaria. This was fulfilled around 732 BC, when Assyria took Damascus.
The Lord speaks to Isaiah again.
The people reject the gentle waters of Shiloah — Jerusalem’s quiet water supply, symbolizing God’s calm care — and admire the kings of Syria and Israel instead.

f.g: A gently flowing channel supplying Jerusalem; compare the later pool of Siloam.

n: So God will bring the mighty river — the king of Assyria — flooding over its banks. Rejecting quiet waters brings a flood.
Assyria will sweep through Judah up to the neck — nearly drowning it, but not completely (Jerusalem survived in 701 BC). Its spreading wings cover “thy land, O Immanuel.”

f.w: he shall reach even to the neck

n: Isaiah taunts the nations: band together, arm yourselves — you will still be shattered.

f.g: Prepare for battle by fastening your belts.

n: Make plans — they will fail; give orders — they won’t stand, “for God is with us” (Immanuel).
With a firm hand, God warned Isaiah not to follow the people’s way of thinking.
Don’t call everything a conspiracy as the people do, and don’t share their fears.
Instead, treat the Lord as holy; let Him be the one you fear and revere.

f.w: Sanctify the Lord of Hosts himself

n: For those who trust Him, the Lord is a sanctuary. For those who don’t, He becomes a stumbling stone and a trap. The New Testament applies this to Christ.
Many will stumble, fall, be broken, snared, and captured.
Isaiah tells his followers to bind up and seal his testimony and teaching, preserving it for the future.
Isaiah will wait for the Lord, even while He hides His face from Israel.

f.w: I will wait upon the Lord

n: Isaiah and his sons, with their symbolic names (Isaiah = “the Lord saves”), are living signs from God.

f.w: I and the children whom the Lord hath given me

n: When people tell you to consult mediums and spiritists who whisper and mutter, ask: shouldn’t people seek their God? The Book of Mormon reads “for the living to hear from the dead?” — a slightly clearer question than the KJV.

f.g: Spirits of the dead supposedly contacted by mediums.
Chirp and whisper — the sounds of spiritist practices.

n: Turn to God’s law and testimony. Anyone who speaks contrary to it has no light.

f.w: To the law and to the testimony

n: Those who reject God will wander distressed and hungry, then curse their king and God as they look upward.
Looking around they will see only trouble, darkness, and anguish, and be thrust into deep gloom. The next chapter answers this darkness with a great light.
